rationale: The student wrote 513 for 37 + 26 because they didn't regroup the 13 ones into 1 ten and 3 ones. The place-value / make-a-ten tool directly visualizes grouping ten ones into a ten rod, showing that a pile of ones over 9 cannot stay in the ones place.

script.focus: ten ones bundling into one ten

intent: Demonstrate make-a-ten on the place-value with values [14]. Tutor points at: ten ones bundling into one ten

frames.caption: Here are 14 ones. That is too many for the ones place: it can only hold 0 to 9.
Bundle ten of them. Ten ones make one ten, so the bundle moves to the tens place. 4 ones are left.
Write 1 in the tens place and 4 in the ones place: 14. One digit per place.

judgement.reasoning: The student wrote 513 for 37 + 26 because they do not understand that only one digit can go in the ones column and that ten ones must be bundled into a ten. This demo explicitly isolates the prerequisite misconception using 14 ones, showing that the ones place can only hold 0 to 9, bundling ten into one ten, and recording one digit per place.
judgement.verdict: Yes, a teacher would definitely use this clear, focused demonstration to show why two digits cannot sit in the ones place and how bundling works.
